title: Book 4 — Melpomene, Chapter 195
paragraphs: Opposite these people, the Carthaginians say, lies an island called Cyrauis, two hundred furlongs long but narrow, which one can walk to from the mainland; and it is full of olives and vines. On it, they say, there is a pool from which the native girls, using birds' feathers smeared with pitch, bring up gold-dust out of the mud. Whether this is actually so I do not know, but I write what is reported; and nothing is impossible—for in Zacynthus too I myself saw pitch brought up out of a pool of water. There are several pools there, the largest measuring seventy feet each way and two fathoms deep. Into it they plunge a pole with a myrtle-branch tied to it, and with the myrtle-branch they bring up pitch, which has the smell of asphalt but is in other respects superior to the pitch of Pieria. They pour this into a pit dug near the pool; and when they have collected a large quantity, they pour it from the pit into jars; and whatever falls into the pool passes underground and reappears in the sea, about four furlongs away. So the report about the island lying near the coast of Libya is also probably true.
